subject: brain
topic: Your sense of free will is a post-hoc narrative construction
angle: While the readiness potential precedes reported decisions, research suggests it is not causal of conscious willing and its link to free will remains unclear.
title: The Construction of Choice

hooks.text: Do you choose your next move?
You think you decide. Your brain starts first.
You are narrating your own movements.
A hand reaching for a glass.
Your sense of will is a construction.

reveal.headline: Neural activity precedes your decision to move.
reveal.body: The readiness potential is a slow buildup of electrical potential associated with movement preparation. It occurs before you report making a choice.

explain.headline: The link to free will is unclear.
explain.body: Neither the readiness potential nor the LRP index are causal of conscious willing. They seem unrelated to your conscious intentions to move.

matters.headline: The narrative of choice may be a construction.
matters.body: Your brain prepares for movement before you feel like you decided to act. That may be why your sense of free will feels like a story your mind tells after the fact.

example.headline: Reaching for a glass of water.
example.body: You sit in a dark kitchen at night. Your hand moves toward the glass. You feel like you chose to reach, but the electrical signals started before the thought arrived.

claims.quote: Both potentials seem unrelated to conscious intentions to move.

claims.text: The link between the Libet paradigm and free will or moral responsibility is not clear.
claims.quote: While the Libet paradigm may be useful for examining how stimuli affect temporal judgments, the link between this and free will or moral responsibility is not clear.

claims.text: The readiness potential (RP) is a slow buildup of electrical potential recorded at the scalp using electroencephalography that is associated with neural activity involved in movement preparation.
claims.quote: The readiness potential (RP), a slow buildup of electrical potential recorded at the scalp using electroencephalography, has been associated with neural activity involved in movement preparation.

claims.text: The readiness potential (RP) precedes the reported time of decision to act by a few hundred milliseconds.
claims.quote: cognitive neuroscientists such as Benjamin Libet have joined the discussion by demonstrating that an ERP component, the readiness potential (RP), precedes the reported time of decision to act by a few hundred milliseconds.

verdict: The evidence shows that the readiness potential is associated with movement preparation but is not a causal driver of conscious intention.
caveat: The exact nature of the neural processes involved in these potentials remains unclear.
caption:
Your sense of free will might be a post-hoc narrative construction.

Research shows that neural activity associated with movement preparation precedes the reported time of decision. However, these processes are not causal of conscious willing, and the exact nature of these processes remains unclear.
